growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: two tiny round cotyledons on wet mud or moss, then toothed rounded leaves that are glossy and sticky when young. Saplings shoot up to about 1 m a year as a straight stem with a narrow conical crown of dark green, blunt- or notch-tipped leaves and stalked purplish buds. After cutting or beaver damage it becomes a multi-stemmed clump of straight poles.
growth.source: European Atlas of Forest Tree Species (normally 10-25 m, exceptionally 35-40 m; lives ~60 yr, up to 160; heart rot after ~60 yr); Claessens et al. 2010 (Forestry 83) abstract: growth very fast to age 7-10, then slows rapidly; Wikipedia (seedlings need light; coppices to straight poles). Height-age and first seed (open trees ~10 yr) estimated.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia / European Atlas: catkins formed the previous autumn open in early spring before bud burst; reddish pendulous male catkins 5-10 cm; female catkins ripen into hard, woody, dark brown to black cone-like fruits 1-3 cm that shed floating winged nutlets mostly through winter to spring. Cluster size, crop and rot times estimated.
